findings.title: VU#102648 - Code injection vulnerability in binary-parser library
findings.summary_md: CERT/CC recorded an earlier code injection flaw in binary-parser before 2.3.0, tracked as CVE-2026-1245, where field names and encoding parameters supplied by an application were interpolated into runtime generated JavaScript without validation. The note says static, hardcoded parser definitions are not affected and that arbitrary JavaScript would run with the privileges of the Node.js process. It credits reporter Maor Caplan and Keichi Takahashi, advises upgrading to 2.3.0, and was last revised on 2026-01-21.

findings.title: Code injection via string options in binary-parser
findings.summary_md: Maintainer Keichi published GHSA-xmxc-6c22-m377 stating that the fix for CVE-2026-1245 validated field names and encodings but left other string options interpolated verbatim into generated parser source. The affected options are length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset and the alias passed to namely(); parsing untrusted binary data with a trusted parser definition is not affected. Version 2.3.1 validates these values as identifier paths and rejects expressions, with CVSS v3.1 scored 8.1 and the finder credited as Zachariah Mithani.

findings.title: Release v2.3.1 · keichi/binary-parser
findings.summary_md: The v2.3.1 release notes describe the security fix for GHSA-xmxc-6c22-m377 and list the affected string options, including length on string, buffer, array, wrapped and seek parsers. The release is a breaking change: those options now accept only identifier paths such as foo or $parent.len, and expressions such as len - 1 are rejected at compile time in favor of a function.

findings.title: CVE-2026-134814: binary-parser before 2.3.1 Code Injection via String-Typed Parser Options
findings.summary_md: The VulnCheck CNA record for CVE-2026-134814 was published on 2026-11-22 at 21:22 UTC and lists a public date of 2026-11-11. It scores CVSS v4.0 at 9.2 and v3.1 at 8.1, affects binary-parser versions below 2.3.1, and credits Zachariah Mithani of AploSec. The record points to the maintainer advisory and two patch commits as references.
